sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Ansar Allah Health Ministry via AP (T1), Nov 7] Airstrikes hit homes in al-Shariya village, Bani Hushaysh district, ~15km northeast of Sanaa, on Saturday, killing at least 25 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children -- up from the 22 killed the same spokesman gave AP earlier Saturday (recorded 1700-02). Alasbahi told Al-Masirah at least 25 were killed. He said civilians were still buried under rubble and that subsequent strikes targeted emergency workers as they tried to pull survivors from the wreckage. Saba reported renewed Saudi strikes against houses and paramedics in the same area, without a casualty figure. Al-Masirah TV footage showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children from ambulances at a local hospital. AP could not independently verify the claims; Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately respond. [CONTEXT] Friday's al-Hadara market strike in Taiz killed at least 30 (Ansar Allah officials); the Ansar Allah and the Saudi-backed Yemeni military blame each other -- neither side's claim independently verified.
sections.what_verified: 1 declared-tier family: AP (T1) carries the updated 25 figure (AAP, The Week, Vartha Bharati, MFC, Ottumwa Courier are AP-wire copies -- same family). Al-Masirah (no declared tier in the registry -- attribution only, never counts) carried the spokesman's update. Primary-source exception applies: the toll is the ministry's own figure.
sections.what_disputed: Saudi Arabia has not commented on the strikes or the toll; AP could not independently verify. The 22->25 rise comes from the same single source (the ministry spokesman) updating his own count as bodies were recovered -- not from independent confirmation. Economic Times / Times of India / Daily Sabah / La Nacion still carry the earlier 22 figure in copies not yet updated.
sections.why_matters: The Sanaa toll just rose to 25 -- and the second wave hit the paramedics digging survivors out of the rubble.

The fault line our audience is arguing over: Saudi bombs on civilian homes -- or Ansar Allah human shields? Who is responsible for Yemen's dead children? New edge: follow-up strikes on the rescuers themselves.
